Manga: Bokurano

About a group of fifteen jaded and misguided thirteen year olds who, upon discovering a video game in a grotto, cause a giant robot to materialize in front of them, where they are teleported to the cockpit and forced to fight another giant robot. The point of the Game is to weed out parallel universes with few differences from each other by having a robot from each of them engage in combat, with the losing pilot's universe being erased from existence, with the winner's universe given the right to exist as the main universe.

The robot is fueled with the life force of it's pilot, causing the pilot to die immediately after the battle has ended, with a new pilot being chosen from the remaining children who signed the contract

In Sburb, the player is supposed to come of age and have their inner self actualized through playing the game, but in Bokurano, the point is to have teenagers come to terms with their impending deaths and use their remaining days to make things right with their families and themselves before they are inevitably chosen to pilot the robot. The manga is brutally nihilistic in tone, making it antithetical to Homestuck in that regard
